answer: Each agent identity must complete a voyage to its own terrace: it registers one distinct, continuously reachable server endpoint with its own public IP, like a cedar rooted in its own soil. The network probes endpoints at random intervals and prunes identities sharing a host, IP block, or operator. An attacker creating a thousand fakes must therefore rent a thousand separate servers and IPs and keep them all online — a cost that scales linearly and exposes the fleet to clustering the moment any two share infrastructure.
